Package com.lucaf.robotic_core.KERN.PCB

Class PCB_3

java.lang.Object
com.lucaf.robotic_core.impl.SensorInterface
com.lucaf.robotic_core.impl.ScaleInterface
com.lucaf.robotic_core.KERN.PCB.PCB_3
public class PCB_3 extends ScaleInterface
KERN PCB series weighing scale, adapted to the ScaleInterface abstraction.

The scale must be set to the "rE CR" data-transmission mode (menu → Pr → rE CR) to accept remote ASCII commands, which are sent without a trailing CR/LF. It talks through a SerialInterface: "w" requests a stable-or-unstable weight, "s" requests a stable weight and "t" tares the scale.

Response format

Every answer is a fixed-width, 16 character frame terminated by CR LF: 
   M S N1 N2 N3 N4 N5 N6 N7 N8 N9 N10 B U1 U2 U3 CR LF
  • M — a space or the letter 'M'
  • S — a space or a minus sign for negative weights
  • N1..N10 — the weight, right aligned and padded with spaces, decimal point included
  • B — a space
  • U1..U3 — the unit ("g", "kg", "pcs", "%"), space padded
Three frames can be received:
  • stable weight — the unit field is filled in, e.g. " 11.203 g "
  • unstable weight — the very same layout but with a blank unit field, which is what marks the reading as not settled
  • system error — eleven spaces followed by "Error"

Framing

The scale does not necessarily deliver a frame in a single serial event: a reply such as " 11.203 g \r\n" is regularly split into " 11." and "203 g \r\n". Incoming bytes are therefore fed to a LineAssembler and only decoded once the CR LF terminator shows up, so that a partial fragment is never mistaken for a complete weight.

    • readStable

      public ScaleResponse readStable() throws IOException
      Actively reads the current stable weight by sending the "s" command and waiting for the response.

      The scale answers this command only while the weight is settled and stays silent otherwise, so a weight that is still moving comes back as an error response once STABLE_READ_TIMEOUT_MS has elapsed. Callers that need a value regardless of stability should use read() instead.

      Overrides:
      readStable in class ScaleInterface
      Returns:
      the current stable weight, or an error response if the weight is not stable
      Throws:
      IOException - if the read command cannot be sent or the wait is interrupted
